chapters.title: Foundations of Context Engineering
chapters.summary: Establishes how context windows, grounding, memory, dynamic facts, and structured context shape AI behavior.

videos.title: Why AI Models Guess Wrong
videos.description: AI guesses go wrong when a task requires exact current values that were not provided in the context.
videos.concept: Root cause of guessing: missing exact current values

figure.alt: Diagnostic comparison showing stable instructions with missing dynamic facts on one side and exact current values on the other, leading to failure versus success.

videos.title: How Context Engineering Bounds AI
videos.description: A request becomes reliable when it is bounded by role, rules, evidence, memory, current facts, and output format.
videos.concept: Context package as the bounded working environment for AI

figure.alt: Diagram showing a central request surrounded by role, rules, evidence, memory, current facts, and output format inside a context package boundary.

videos.title: How AI Context Windows Actually Work
videos.description: The context window is finite working memory, so rules, tasks, facts, examples, and history must compete for limited space.
videos.concept: Finite working memory and token-budget trade-offs

figure.alt: Infographic showing a finite context window with a token budget and labeled blocks for rules, task, relevant facts, examples, and chat history, plus overflow items outside the window.

videos.title: How to Pack a Context Window
videos.description: When the window is limited, the best context package prioritizes the highest-value information and leaves lower-value material out.
videos.concept: Priority-based packing under capacity constraints

figure.alt: Suitcase-style infographic showing a context window packed by priority with optional background and extra history left out.

videos.title: How the Context Skeleton Fixes AI Prompts
videos.description: A reusable context skeleton replaces a mixed prompt with an organized structure that is clearer, more complete, and more repeatable.
videos.concept: Structured context skeleton

figure.alt: Before-and-after diagram showing a messy prompt on the left and a clean context skeleton with labeled sections on the right.

videos.title: How Grounding Stops AI Guessing
videos.description: Providing the smallest sufficient evidence set turns an unsupported guess into a document-grounded answer.
videos.concept: Evidence-to-answer grounding

figure.alt: Two-panel infographic comparing question-only prompting with grounded prompting that includes evidence excerpts and a grounded answer.

videos.title: How to Build an AI Memory Block
videos.description: Useful AI memory is a compact block that carries forward the signal—such as summary, pinned facts, and next steps—without dragging along the full history.
videos.concept: Compact controlled memory block

figure.alt: Infographic showing a noisy raw conversation compressed into a compact AI memory block with rolling summary, pinned facts, and next steps.

videos.title: How the Dynamic Facts Block Fixes AI
videos.description: Stable policy becomes actionable when current case-specific data is added in a dedicated Dynamic Facts block.
videos.concept: Stable policy plus current dynamic facts

figure.alt: Two-row infographic showing a stable policy combined with missing versus current dynamic facts, leading to outdated versus accurate AI answers.

chapters.title: The Context Engineering Lifecycle
chapters.summary: Presents a lifecycle for discovering, selecting, shaping, executing, evaluating, iterating, and deploying context.

videos.title: The Context Engineering Lifecycle: From Gut Feel to Reliable AI
videos.description: The seven-phase lifecycle turns prompt work into a controlled loop with visible decisions, reviewable evidence, and continuous improvement.
videos.concept: Seven-phase controlled lifecycle loop

figure.alt: Circular lifecycle diagram showing Discovery, Selection, Shaping, Execution, Evaluation, Iteration, and Deployment around a controlled loop for reliable AI.

videos.title: Discovery: Define the Job Before You Write the Prompt
videos.description: Discovery converts a vague AI idea into a bounded task with explicit users, allowed sources, constraints, success criteria, and representative test cases.
videos.concept: Define the job and success before prompt refinement

figure.alt: Discovery checklist and artifact panel showing key questions, problem statement, user definition, success rubric, representative test cases, and context inventory.

videos.title: Selection: Choose the Highest-Signal Context
videos.description: Selection classifies information as always fit, usually fit, or optional while excluding noise and redundancy.
videos.concept: Select highest-signal context

figure.alt: Three-level funnel showing Always Fit, Usually Fit, and Optional context, plus a decision question about relevance and noise.

videos.title: Shaping: Turn Selected Information Into an Operational Prompt
videos.description: Shaping organizes selected information into labeled blocks so the workflow is clear, reusable, reviewable, and easier to diagnose.
videos.concept: Structure selected content into an operational prompt

figure.alt: Context skeleton panel transforming selected information into a well-shaped prompt with labeled role, rules, evidence, dynamic facts, memory, task, and output format blocks.

videos.title: Execution: Test Representative Cases, Not Just the Easy One
videos.description: Execution tests typical, edge, and failure cases consistently and captures outputs as reproducible evidence.
videos.concept: Test representative cases consistently

figure.alt: Execution panel showing typical, edge, and failure test cases alongside goals to run consistently and capture outputs.

videos.title: Evaluation: Score the Output Against a Rubric, Not a Feeling
videos.description: Evaluation separates accuracy, completeness, grounding, constraint adherence, and usability so hidden tradeoffs become visible.
videos.concept: Score outputs with a multi-dimensional rubric

figure.alt: Evaluation rubric panel showing five criteria and example scores for typical, edge, and failure cases.

videos.title: Iteration: Change One Variable and Re-test the Same Cases
videos.description: Controlled iteration changes one meaningful variable, reruns the same cases, and measures improvement without guessing.
videos.concept: Targeted one-variable iteration with regression testing

figure.alt: Iteration panel showing one variable changed at a time and the same typical, edge, and failure cases re-tested.

videos.title: Deployment: Launch Is the Start of Maintenance
videos.description: Deployment assigns ownership, monitoring, review, and update responsibilities so the workflow remains reliable as conditions change.
videos.concept: Continuous maintenance after launch

figure.alt: Deployment panel showing monitoring, feedback, source and policy updates, re-testing, and a maintain-and-improve loop.

chapters.title: Designing High-Quality Contexts
chapters.summary: Explains how relevance, authority, freshness, ordering, state, and signal-to-noise produce higher-quality contexts.

videos.title: What Makes Context High Quality?
videos.description: High-quality context is relevant, authoritative, fresh, clear, explicit about precedence, low-noise, and fit for purpose.
videos.concept: Seven-point context-quality test

figure.alt: A central context package surrounded by seven quality checks: relevant, authoritative, fresh, clear, precedence, low noise, and fit for purpose.

videos.title: The Relevance Filter: Does This Information Change the Answer?
videos.description: The removal test protects the smallest sufficient evidence set by retaining only information that changes the answer, constraints, key facts, or output structure.
videos.concept: Relevance filtering and smallest sufficient evidence

figure.alt: Candidate context passes through a removal-test funnel, producing a smallest sufficient set containing approved policy, current status, and a decision summary.

videos.title: Authority and Freshness: Which Source Should Win?
videos.description: Source control uses owner, effective date, version, and source-of-record status to resolve conflicts instead of leaving the model to choose silently.
videos.concept: Authority, freshness, and explicit precedence

figure.alt: Two conflicting sources—an old email and a current policy—are compared using owner, effective date, version, and source-of-record checks; the current policy wins.

videos.title: Signal-to-Noise: Why More Context Can Reduce Quality
videos.description: Removing redundant, stale, and merely related material increases the useful signal without stripping away required support.
videos.concept: Signal-to-noise discipline and selective reduction

figure.alt: A bloated context containing many unrelated blocks passes through a filter and becomes a compact high-signal set with the rule, exception process, current facts, escalation contact, and output format.

videos.title: The Context Envelope: Package the Task So the Model Can Read It
videos.description: A context envelope separates role, rules, reference, dynamic facts, task, output, and checks into a legible operating package.
videos.concept: Legible context envelope with labeled boundaries

figure.alt: A large context envelope contains seven labeled sections: role, rules, reference, dynamic facts, task, output, and checks.

videos.title: Ordering and Precedence: Put the Right Information in Control
videos.description: A visible order and explicit conflict rules make it clear how behavior, evidence, current facts, the task, and the output contract relate.
videos.concept: Visible hierarchy and explicit conflict resolution

figure.alt: A numbered prompt stack shows role, rules, reference, dynamic facts, task, output, and checks; beside it, three precedence rules show policy over user request, current evidence over stale notes, and current facts over remembered assumptions.

videos.title: Current-State Control: Stop Letting Yesterday Answer Today
videos.description: Durable guidance stays separate from a compact Dynamic Facts block containing labels, sources, timestamps, and refresh triggers.
videos.concept: Dynamic facts and refresh discipline

figure.alt: Approved durable guidance is combined with a dynamic facts area comparing stale values with a refreshed block containing a source, timestamp, and before-each-run refresh trigger.

videos.title: From Personal Prompt to Organizational Asset
videos.description: A shared context asset documents purpose, approved sources, ownership, versioning, tests, review rules, refresh cadence, and escalation.
videos.concept: Reusable, reviewable, maintainable context asset

figure.alt: A personal prompt with hidden assumptions and manual correction transforms into an organizational asset containing purpose, approved sources, labeled sections, owner, version, test cases, review rules, refresh cadence, and escalation path.

chapters.title: Reliability, Failure Handling, and Measurement
chapters.summary: Shows how to diagnose failures, apply focused mitigations, test reliability, and protect working behavior from regressions.

videos.title: One Good Answer Does Not Prove Reliability
videos.description: A single strong answer demonstrates possibility, but reliability requires acceptable behavior across representative cases, users, and changing conditions over time.
videos.concept: Reliability across cases and time

figure.alt: Infographic contrasting one successful AI demo with broader reliability across routine cases, edge cases, missing information, conflicting instructions, different users, and changing conditions.

videos.title: The First Five Reliability Triage Checks
videos.description: Before editing a prompt, diagnose the observable symptom, confirm the source of truth, inspect grounding, review instruction quality, and check format and history effects.
videos.concept: Initial reliability triage sequence

figure.alt: Five-step reliability triage infographic showing observable symptom, source of truth, missing facts or grounding, instruction quality, and format/history effects.

videos.title: Hallucination Is a Symptom — Diagnose the Cause
videos.description: Unsupported output should be treated as a symptom and traced to missing evidence, ambiguity, stale sources, conflicting instructions, or pressure to answer without enough support.
videos.concept: Cause-specific diagnosis of unsupported output

figure.alt: Cause-and-mitigation diagram for hallucinations, linking missing evidence, ambiguous questions, stale sources, conflicting instructions, and answer pressure to specific fixes.

videos.title: Prompt Injection: Treat Retrieved Text as Untrusted Input
videos.description: Retrieved or user-supplied content must remain clearly separated from trusted governing instructions so the model analyzes the data without obeying it.
videos.concept: Trust boundary between instructions and untrusted data

figure.alt: Trust-boundary infographic separating trusted governing instructions from untrusted external content, with practical controls and output validation checks.

videos.title: Use the Smallest Credible Mitigation
videos.description: Fix the diagnosed failure with the smallest change that credibly addresses the root cause, then rerun the same case and check for regressions.
videos.concept: Focused mitigation without creating reliability debt

figure.alt: Process infographic showing symptom identification, root-cause isolation, minimal fix, rerun of the same case, and standing-suite regression check.

videos.title: Build a Test Suite Before You Trust the Workflow
videos.description: A reliable workflow pairs the prompt with a representative test suite covering routine, edge, missing-information, policy-pressure, untrusted-input, and format-stability cases.
videos.concept: Representative test suites as reliability evidence

figure.alt: Blueprint infographic for an AI prompt test suite, showing prompt plus test suite, case categories, a good case schema, and coverage versus raw volume.

videos.title: Regression Testing: Do Not Trade Safety for Polish
videos.description: Compare the candidate version against a protected baseline on the same cases and rubric, then classify each behavior as improved, held, tradeoff, or weakened.
videos.concept: Protected baselines and regression decisions

figure.alt: Regression testing infographic showing a protected baseline, standing test suite, candidate revision, behavior classifications, and release decisions.

videos.title: Format Drift: When the Answer Is Right but Unusable
videos.description: Structure is part of correctness when headings, fields, keys, ordering, or length must remain stable for reviewers, forms, and downstream systems.
videos.concept: Format stability as an operational requirement

figure.alt: Comparison infographic showing correct facts in a broken format versus the same facts in the right structure, plus controls to prevent format drift.

chapters.title: Enterprise Operationalization
chapters.summary: Moves AI workflows from prototypes toward governed enterprise operation across privacy, policy, security, release, and fail-safe design.

videos.title: A Successful Prototype Is Not Enterprise Ready
videos.description: A working demo proves possibility, but enterprise readiness requires privacy, policy, safety, security, performance, release discipline, monitoring, and fail-safe behavior.
videos.concept: Prototype success versus governed enterprise readiness

figure.alt: Comparison infographic showing prototype success versus enterprise readiness across eight readiness lanes including privacy, policy, safety, security, performance, release, monitoring, and fail-safe behavior.

videos.title: Context Selection Is a Privacy Decision
videos.description: Need-to-know context selection reduces exposure by classifying data, removing unnecessary fields, masking identifiers, using safer summaries, and defining lifecycle controls.
videos.concept: Need-to-know selection and privacy minimization

figure.alt: Workflow infographic showing how raw data becomes a reduced context package through classification, need-to-know filtering, masking, summarization, and access-retention controls.

videos.title: Policy Blocks: Turn Rules into Operational Assets
videos.description: A concise, named, versioned policy block makes rules explicit, reusable, testable, and clearly higher priority than the user request.
videos.concept: Operational policy blocks and decision hierarchy

figure.alt: Infographic showing an example policy block, policy decision hierarchy, and maintenance flow for versioned policy assets.

videos.title: Prompt Injection and Data Exfiltration: Define the Trust Boundary
videos.description: Trusted instructions must stay separate from untrusted content, with least-privilege access, retrieval boundaries, and output validation checks.
videos.concept: Trust boundary between governed instructions and untrusted input

figure.alt: Security infographic showing a trust boundary between trusted instructions and untrusted input, plus least-privilege controls, retrieval boundaries, and output validation.

videos.title: Version, Test, Stage, and Roll Back
videos.description: Treat prompt, retrieval, policy, and evaluation changes as governed releases with versioning, regression testing, staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback discipline.
videos.concept: Governed releases for AI workflow changes

figure.alt: Release-management infographic showing versioned assets, change log, regression testing, staged rollout, approval gate, rollback triggers, and last stable version.

videos.title: Fail-Safes: Design What Happens When the Workflow Is Uncertain
videos.description: When evidence, tools, or scope are uncertain, enterprise workflows should clarify, refuse, escalate, degrade gracefully, or reset the context package.
videos.concept: Safe exits and graceful degradation under uncertainty

figure.alt: Fail-safe decision infographic mapping common failure conditions to safe exits and outcomes, including clarification, refusal, escalation, conservative fallback, safer subset, and reset.

videos.title: Refusal That Preserves Trust
videos.description: A good refusal states the boundary, gives a brief reason, offers a safe next step, and escalates when needed so the user can still move forward safely.
videos.concept: Trust-preserving refusal pattern

figure.alt: Refusal-pattern infographic showing boundary, brief reason, safe alternative, escalation, examples of safe next steps, and good versus poor refusal behavior.

videos.title: Route by Complexity and Consequence
videos.description: Enterprise routing should balance quality, latency, cost, and review effort by matching stronger controls to higher complexity and higher consequence requests.
videos.concept: Complexity-and-consequence routing

figure.alt: Quadrant infographic routing requests by complexity and consequence, with lean, balanced, and high-control paths and outcome trends for quality, latency, token use, cost, and review workload.
